Probe: ByteForge is building an internal IDE copilot for engineers working on proprietary firmware repos. They are security-first — must be fully air-gapped in prod. Short fragments / call notes below.

- Jan 28 POC kickoff (virtual): demo of Redwood hosted API + discussion of on-prem constraints. CTO: "models cannot phone home; telemetry must be aggregated only."
- Security: want signed offline bundles + installable RPM/OCI tar with SHA256 verification.
- Packaging ask: single offline deliverable that includes runtime, model shards, quantized artifacts, post-installation preflight script, and an offline license key server.
- Hardware sizing: ByteForge expects to support ~50 concurrent dev sessions with streaming completions and <150ms token latency target for IDE flows. Initial ask: recommended sizing draft (see drive doc) — 4x H100 prod cluster, 2x A100 staging, 512GB system RAM per host, 200TB NVMe for models/shards, 10GbE internal network.
- Offline updates: monthly signed model bundles + patch pack; prefer delta patches to reduce transfer time over removable media. Needs documented rollback & integrity checks.
- Telemetry policy: aggregate metrics only (rps, token counts, error rates). NO source snippets, NO stack traces containing code.
- Integration: plugin for internal JetBrains + VS Code; local proxy that pins model version per workspace.
- Cost sensitivity: high at infra level — looking to validate Optimize suggestions (quantization + batching) to reduce GPU footprint.
- Quote from DevOps lead: "We need an installer that our infra team can vet in 48 hours. If it passes, procurement moves fast."
- Current stage: hands-on evaluation with planned onsite install POC (2 weeks).
- Primary risks: procurement window for H100s, corporate legal on offline license language, and clarification on support SLA for air-gapped emergency updates.
